docs.title: VaaniAI
docs.text:
VaaniAI is a voice-first conversational AI assistant built on a FastAPI backend. It accepts speech input directly from the browser, processes it through a local speech-to-text pipeline, reasons over it using an LLM agent equipped with real-time tools, and returns a spoken audio response generated by a local TTS engine.

The assistant can answer general questions, search the web, fetch live weather data, and answer questions grounded in PDF documents you upload — all through a single browser-based interface.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
Speech Recognition (STT) Audio recorded in the browser is sent to the server and transcribed using the OpenAI Whisper API (whisper-1). The language is fixed to English by default.

Conversational AI Agent The VaaniAI agent is built on a custom agentic loop backed by the OpenAI API (default model: gpt-4.1-mini). The agent maintains per-session conversation history and decides autonomously when to invoke tools before generating a final response.

Tool Execution The agent has access to three tools:

  • Web Search — queries the Tavily API for real-time web results
  • Weather — queries the OpenWeatherMap API for current weather conditions
  • PDF Search — performs a hybrid (vector + full-text) search against the active uploaded document

Document Ingestion and RAG PDFs uploaded through the UI are chunked, embedded locally using the all-mpnet-base-v2 SentenceTransformer model (768-dimensional embeddings), and persisted in a PostgreSQL database with the pgvector extension. Documents are identified by their SHA-256 content hash, so re-uploading an identical file skips re-embedding entirely.

Text-to-Speech (TTS) The agent's text response is synthesized into speech using Piper TTS, a local neural TTS engine. The binary and voice model (en_US-lessac-medium) are downloaded automatically on first run. The generated .wav file is served back to the browser for playback.

Web Interface The frontend is a single-page HTML/CSS/JS application served as static files by FastAPI. It uses the browser's native MediaRecorder API to capture microphone input and communicates with the backend via standard fetch calls.

Navigate to Introduction for a detailed breakdown of each component, Technical Design for the architecture and data model, or Local Setup to get the project running.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This page describes how each component of VaaniAI works internally.

docs.title: Speech-to-Text (STT)
docs.text:
Audio is captured in the browser using the native MediaRecorder API. When the user clicks the microphone button, recording begins. Clicking it again stops the recording, and the audio blob (typically .webm or .ogg, depending on the browser) is immediately sent as a file upload to the /api/chat endpoint.

On the server, the uploaded audio is saved to a temporary file (generated/api_temp/user_input.wav) and passed to the AudioTranscriber class. Transcription is performed via the OpenAI Audio Transcriptions API using the whisper-1 model. The language is fixed to English (en). If transcription returns empty text, a system message is injected informing the LLM that no speech was detected, allowing the agent to gracefully ask the user to repeat themselves.

Relevant file: src/backend/assistant/stt/transcriber.py

docs.title: LLM Agent
docs.text:
VaaniAI uses a custom Agent base class (src/backend/llm/agent_core/agent.py) that wraps the OpenAI Chat Completions API with a tool-calling loop. The loop runs up to max_iteration times (default: 3). On each iteration:

  1. The full conversation history is sent to the model.
  2. If the model returns tool_calls, each tool is executed sequentially, and the result is appended back to the conversation history as a role: tool message.
  3. This continues until the model returns a plain text response with no further tool calls.

The VaaniAI class (src/backend/llm/vaani_agent/agent.py) extends this base and is pre-configured with:

  • Model: gpt-4.1-mini
  • Temperature: 0.5
  • System Prompt: Instructs the agent on its role, available tools, and output format. The prompt is defined in src/backend/llm/vaani_agent/prompt.py.

Conversation history across turns is managed by ConversationManager (src/backend/llm/agent_core/conversation.py), which keeps the last 10 messages in memory (excluding the system prompt) to avoid exceeding token limits.

docs.title: Web Search
docs.text:
The web search tool uses the Tavily Python client (tavily-python) to perform a basic depth search and return up to 3 results. Each result includes a title, URL, and a content snippet. Results are formatted as a plain-text string and returned to the agent.

Requires: TAVILY_API_KEY in .env Relevant file: src/backend/llm/tools/web_search.py

docs.title: Weather
docs.text:
The weather tool queries the OpenWeatherMap API (/data/2.5/weather) using httpx. It takes a location string (e.g., "London, UK"), fetches current conditions, and returns a formatted string including city, country, condition, temperature (Celsius), and humidity.

Requires: WEATHERAPI_KEY in .env Relevant file: src/backend/llm/tools/weather.py

docs.title: PDF Search (RAG)
docs.text:
The PDF search tool calls pdf_store.search(), which encodes the query using the same SentenceTransformer model used during ingestion, then delegates to db_manager.search_chunks(). Search is scoped to the currently active document by its SHA-256 hash.

Relevant files: src/backend/llm/tools/pdf_search.py, src/backend/llm/rag/pdf_store.py

docs.title: PDF Ingestion Pipeline
docs.text:
When a user uploads a PDF via the /api/upload-pdf endpoint, the following happens:

  1. The file's SHA-256 hash is computed from its byte content.
  2. If a document with that hash already exists in the database, processing is skipped entirely and the document is set as active immediately ("cache hit").
  3. If the hash is new, the PDF is saved temporarily and processed:
  4. Text is extracted page by page using pypdf.
  5. Each page is split on double newlines (\n\n). If a page has fewer than two chunks and its text exceeds 1,000 characters, it is re-chunked into 500-character fixed-size segments instead.
  6. Each chunk and its page number and filename are recorded as metadata.
  7. All chunks are encoded in a single batch using SentenceTransformer("all-mpnet-base-v2") to produce 768-dimensional float vectors.
  8. The chunks, metadata, embeddings, and file hash are saved to the document_chunks table in PostgreSQL.
  9. The server streams status messages back to the frontend during processing via StreamingResponse.

Relevant file: src/backend/llm/rag/pdf_store.py

docs.title: Hybrid Search
docs.text:
When the agent calls execute_pdf_search, the system runs two parallel searches against the document_chunks table, filtered to the active file_hash:

  • Vector search: ranks chunks by cosine distance between the query embedding and stored embeddings, retrieving the top 10.
  • Full-text search (FTS): uses PostgreSQL's plainto_tsquery and to_tsvector (English dictionary) to find and rank lexically matching chunks, retrieving the top 10.

The two result sets are merged using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with a constant k=60. Each chunk receives a combined score of 1/(k + rank + 1) from each list it appears in. The top top_k (default: 3) chunks by combined score are returned to the agent.

Relevant file: src/backend/database/db_manager.py

docs.title: Text-to-Speech (TTS)
docs.text:
After the agent produces its final text response, TextToSpeech.speak() is called. It invokes the Piper binary as a subprocess, passing the response text via stdin. Piper writes a .wav file to generated/api_temp/agent_output.wav.

The VoiceManager handles finding the Piper executable and voice model. If either is missing on startup, it is downloaded automatically:

  • The Piper binary is downloaded from the official GitHub releases page for the detected OS (Windows, Linux, or macOS).
  • The voice model (en_US-lessac-medium) is fetched from the rhasspy/piper-voices Hugging Face repository using huggingface_hub. An HF_TOKEN is required.

When USE_BROWSER_AUDIO=True (the default), speak() returns the path to the generated .wav file rather than playing it locally. The FastAPI endpoint then serves this file via the /api/audio/{filename} route, and the frontend plays it through an <audio> element.

Relevant files: src/backend/assistant/tts/speaker.py, src/backend/assistant/tts/voice_manager.py

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.14 or newer
  • PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension installed
  • A Hugging Face account (needed to download the Piper TTS voice model on first run)

docs.title: 1. Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Akshumishra/VaaniAI.git
cd VaaniAI

docs.title: 2. Install dependencies with uv
docs.text:
uv will create a .venv virtual environment and install all packages from pyproject.toml.

uv sync

Activate the environment:

# Windows
.venv\Scripts\activate

# macOS / Linux
source .venv/bin/activate

docs.title: 3. Configure environment variables
docs.text:
Copy .env.sample to .env and fill in your values:

cp .env.sample .env

Open .env and set the following:

HF_TOKEN=your_hugging_face_access_token
OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_api_key
TAVILY_API_KEY=your_tavily_api_key
WEATHERAPI_KEY=your_weatherapi_key
LOG_LEVEL=INFO
USE_BROWSER_AUDIO=True

Variable notes:

  • OPENAI_API_KEY — used for both speech transcription (Whisper) and LLM reasoning. Required.
  • DATABASE_URL — defaults to postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres. Override if your PostgreSQL setup differs.
  • HF_TOKEN — required only for the first run to download the Piper voice model from Hugging Face. After the model is cached locally under models/piper/, it is no longer needed at runtime.
  • TAVILY_API_KEY — required only if you want the web search tool to function.
  • WEATHERAPI_KEY — this is an OpenWeatherMap API key, required only if you want the weather tool to function.
  • USE_BROWSER_AUDIO — set to True (the default) when using the web UI. Set to False only if running without a browser and you want audio played through local system speakers.

docs.title: 4. Set up the database
docs.text:
Ensure PostgreSQL is running and the pgvector extension is available. The application will create the document_chunks table automatically on first startup via SQLAlchemy.

To install pgvector on your PostgreSQL instance (if not already done):

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;

docs.title: 5. Run the application
docs.text:
Start the FastAPI server:

uvicorn src.backend.api.main:app --reload

Open your browser and navigate to:

http://localhost:8000

The first time the server starts, it will download the Piper binary and the en_US-lessac-medium voice model if they are not already present in bin/ and models/piper/. This may take a minute depending on your connection speed.

docs.title: Running the Documentation Site
docs.text:
To preview this documentation locally:

uv run mkdocs serve

Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:8000 (or http://127.0.0.1:8001 if the app server is already running on port 8000).

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text:
The diagram below shows the high-level component layout of VaaniAI.

graph TD
    Browser["Browser (Frontend)"]

    subgraph FastAPI Backend
        API["API Layer\n(src/backend/api/main.py)"]
        STT["AudioTranscriber\n(OpenAI Whisper API)"]
        Agent["VaaniAI Agent\n(gpt-4.1-mini)"]
        TTS["TextToSpeech\n(Piper TTS)"]
        ConvMgr["ConversationManager"]

        subgraph Tools
            WebSearch["Web Search\n(Tavily)"]
            Weather["Weather\n(OpenWeatherMap)"]
            PDFSearch["PDF Search\n(RAG)"]
        end

        subgraph RAG Pipeline
            PDFStore["PDFStore\n(SentenceTransformer)"]
            DBMgr["DatabaseManager\n(Hybrid Search)"]
        end
    end

    PostgreSQL[("PostgreSQL\n+ pgvector\ndocument_chunks")]

    Browser -- "POST /api/chat (audio)" --> API
    Browser -- "POST /api/upload-pdf (pdf)" --> API
    API --> STT
    STT --> Agent
    Agent --> ConvMgr
    Agent --> WebSearch
    Agent --> Weather
    Agent --> PDFSearch
    PDFSearch --> PDFStore
    PDFStore --> DBMgr
    API --> PDFStore
    DBMgr <--> PostgreSQL
    Agent --> TTS
    TTS -- "GET /api/audio/..." --> Browser

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
The FastAPI application is defined in src/backend/api/main.py. It exposes three endpoints:

Method Path Description POST /api/chat Receives a .wav audio upload, transcribes it, runs the agent, returns text and audio URL GET /api/audio/{filename} Serves the generated TTS .wav file POST /api/upload-pdf Receives a PDF, computes its hash, ingests it if new, streams status text back

The frontend HTML/JS/CSS is served under / via FastAPI's StaticFiles mount.

docs.title: Voice Chat Turn
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Browser
    participant API as FastAPI API
    participant STT as AudioTranscriber
    participant LLM as VaaniAI Agent
    participant Tool as Tool (optional)
    participant TTS as TextToSpeech

    Browser->>API: POST /api/chat (audio blob)
    API->>API: Save to user_input.wav
    API->>STT: transcribe(audio_path)
    STT->>STT: OpenAI Whisper API call
    STT-->>API: Transcribed text

    API->>LLM: invoke(conversation_history)
    loop Agent loop (max 10 iterations)
        LLM->>LLM: Call OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini
        alt Tool call requested
            LLM->>Tool: execute tool (web_search / weather / pdf_search)
            Tool-->>LLM: Tool result appended to history
        else Plain text response
            LLM-->>API: Final response text
        end
    end

    API->>TTS: speak(response_text, output_path)
    TTS->>TTS: Run Piper subprocess
    TTS-->>API: Path to agent_output.wav

    API-->>Browser: { user_text, assistant_text, audio_url }
    Browser->>API: GET /api/audio/agent_output.wav
    API-->>Browser: WAV file
    Browser->>Browser: Play audio

docs.title: PDF Upload and Ingestion
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Browser
    participant API as FastAPI API
    participant PDFStore
    participant DB as DatabaseManager
    participant PG as PostgreSQL

    Browser->>API: POST /api/upload-pdf (pdf file)
    API->>API: Compute SHA-256 hash

    API->>DB: check_document_exists(hash)
    DB->>PG: Query document_chunks WHERE file_hash = hash
    PG-->>DB: Result

    alt Hash already exists (cache hit)
        DB-->>API: True
        API->>PDFStore: Set active_file_hash
        API-->>Browser: Stream "Document already processed. Ready."
    else New document
        DB-->>API: False
        API->>PDFStore: add_pdf_generator(path, hash, filename)
        PDFStore-->>Browser: Stream "Extracting text..."
        PDFStore->>PDFStore: pypdf extracts text per page
        PDFStore->>PDFStore: Chunk text (newline split or 500-char fixed)
        PDFStore-->>Browser: Stream "Generating embeddings..."
        PDFStore->>PDFStore: SentenceTransformer encodes all chunks
        PDFStore->>DB: save_chunks(metadata, chunks, embeddings, hash)
        DB->>PG: INSERT INTO document_chunks
        PG-->>DB: OK
        PDFStore-->>Browser: Stream "Ready."
    end

docs.title: Agent Tool-Calling Loop
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Start([User message received]) --> AddHistory[Add to ConversationManager]
    AddHistory --> CallLLM[Call OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini\nwith full history]
    CallLLM --> HasToolCalls{Tool calls\nin response?}

    HasToolCalls -- Yes --> ExecTool[Execute each tool\nin order]
    ExecTool --> AppendResult[Append tool results\nto history as role:tool]
    AppendResult --> CheckIter{Max iterations\nreached?}
    CheckIter -- No --> CallLLM
    CheckIter -- Yes --> Error([Return error message])

    HasToolCalls -- No --> FinalResponse[Return plain text response]
    FinalResponse --> AddAssistant[Add to conversation history]
    AddAssistant --> TTS([Pass to TextToSpeech])

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text: VaaniAI uses a single PostgreSQL table for RAG storage.

docs.title: Entity Relationship Diagram
docs.text:
erDiagram
    DOCUMENT_CHUNKS {
        integer id PK
        text document_name
        text file_hash
        integer page_number
        text chunk_text
        vector_768 embedding
    }

Notes:

  • file_hash stores the SHA-256 hex digest of the original PDF file's byte content. It is indexed for fast lookups and scopes all search queries to a single document.
  • embedding is a 768-dimensional float vector produced by the all-mpnet-base-v2 SentenceTransformer model, stored via the pgvector extension (Vector(768)).
  • There are no foreign keys. Each row is a self-contained chunk. Documents are identified logically by file_hash, and only one document (the most recently uploaded) is treated as "active" per server session.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All configuration is loaded from environment variables via Settings in src/backend/core/setting.py. The .env file is loaded automatically from the project root.

Variable Required Default Description OPENAI_API_KEY Yes — Used for Whisper transcription and LLM calls DATABASE_URL Yes postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres PostgreSQL connection string HF_TOKEN Yes (first run) — Hugging Face token for downloading the Piper voice model TAVILY_API_KEY Optional — Required for the web search tool WEATHERAPI_KEY Optional — Required for the weather tool (OpenWeatherMap key) LOG_LEVEL Optional INFO Python logging level USE_BROWSER_AUDIO Optional True If True, TTS audio is served over HTTP; if False, played locally via system audio

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text: Component Library / Service Web framework FastAPI + Uvicorn Speech-to-text OpenAI Whisper API (whisper-1) LLM OpenAI Chat Completions API (gpt-4.1-mini) Text-to-speech Piper TTS (en_US-lessac-medium ONNX model) Embeddings sentence-transformers (all-mpnet-base-v2) Vector database PostgreSQL + pgvector ORM SQLAlchemy PDF parsing pypdf Web search Tavily API (tavily-python) Weather OpenWeatherMap API (httpx) Frontend HTML / Vanilla JS / CSS Dependency management uv
